title: All for One, One for All
text:
In Alexandre Dumas's novel, young d'Artagnan arrived in Paris from Gascony in 1625, hoping to join the king's musketeers. On his first morning he managed to offend three musketeers in turn, Athos, Porthos and Aramis, and he agreed to fight each of them in a duel that same day, one after the other, at the same place.

When they had all gathered and Athos and d'Artagnan crossed swords, a patrol of Cardinal Richelieu's guards arrived to arrest them, since dueling was forbidden. The three musketeers were outnumbered, five to three. D'Artagnan had to choose a side, and he chose them. The four fought together and beat the guards. From that day the four were inseparable.

Their friendship was tested again and again. When they rode to England to recover the queen's diamond studs before the cardinal could expose her, they were ambushed one by one along the road. Porthos was left behind after a duel, Aramis was wounded, Athos was trapped in a fight at an inn. Each sacrifice kept d'Artagnan moving, until he reached London with only his servant and brought the studs back in time.

Their motto was a promise each made to the others: all for one, one for all.
lesson: Friends who commit to each other completely can achieve what none could alone. Sometimes being a good teammate means taking the blow so another can carry the mission forward.
source: Alexandre Dumas, The Three Musketeers (Les Trois Mousquetaires), 1844
